_source: real -- measured against Cirrascale AI Suite (https://aisuite.cirrascale.com/apis/v2), OpenAI-shaped /chat/completions, n=2 per point at 16 and 128 max_tokens. Pricing is Cirrascale's published catalogue rate, not a measured invoice. See ../cloud_ai100/_real_endpoint_log.md for the full log, including what is still NOT verifiable (the Cloud AI 100 silicon is not observable through this API).
_model_note: Llama-3.3-70B is the intended deep brain. Measurements below were taken against Llama-3.1-8B, the only catalogue model reachable while the larger ones returned 'Models Busy/Unavailable'. Re-measure when a 70B answers -- expect it to be slower per token.

latency_ms._network_rtt_note: real, but this is fixed overhead (RTT + prefill of a 44-token prompt) derived from the intercept of the 16/128-token fit, not an isolated ping
latency_ms._ttft_note: not separable without streaming; folded into network_rtt_mean above so the router's ttft + n*per_token estimate stays correct

_cost_note: Output rate for the 70B, kept for the legacy single-rate field. Real billing splits input/output and differs per model -- CirrascaleDeepBrain.MODEL_PRICING is the authority. The previous value here was 1.8 USD/1k, a datasheet guess ~2600x too high that made one query look like $1.03; it did not affect routing, since policy.py decides on difficulty and latency budget, not cost.
